bullets.title: Fed's Waller: Rate hike back on table if CPI hot this week
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller warned that another hot core inflation reading could force near-term rate hikes, stating he'd treat such a print as a 'signal, not noise.' He noted inflation has risen in 2026 regardless of measurement method and can no longer be attributed to tariffs. Market repriced July hike odds from 35% to ~50% on his comments; gold fell 3% and Treasuries sold off. Waller also identified AI buildout demand as an upward inflation pressure factor.

bullets.title: TSM: June revenue +68% YoY at $13.79B, beats Q2 guidance; earnings 7/16
bullets.body: TSMC reported June net revenue of NT$442.68B (~$13.79B), up 67.9% YoY and 6.2% MoM, with H1 2026 revenue of $74.99B. Q2 revenue of $40.2B beat the high end of guidance. Options market pricing a 3.57% implied move around the 7/16 earnings print at ~1:30am EDT.

bullets.title: META: UBS cuts PT to $766 from $865; $40B Louisiana data center announced
bullets.body: UBS reduced its META price target by $99 (11.4%) to $766. Separately, Meta announced it will spend more than $40 billion on a Louisiana data center, consistent with the hyperscaler capex supercycle theme. A large block trade also hit the tape during the session.

bullets.title: INTC: €5B Ireland fab investment to scale Intel 3 for Xeon 6 and Diamond Rapids
bullets.body: Intel announced a €5 billion (~$5.7B) investment at its Leixlip Fab 34 in Ireland, targeting Intel 3 node production for Xeon 6 and next-gen Diamond Rapids processors by 2027. Former Intel CEO Patrick Gelsinger, now a director, purchased 153,846 shares for $500K (~$3.25/share), joining other insiders in a $6M combined purchase on the same day.

bullets.title: NVDA: vLLM performance leadership praised; AMD lags; internal compute competition
bullets.body: NVDA's vLLM performance was praised by industry observers while AMD was noted to have 'significant catching up to do' on model optimization. Separately, NVDA's own head of automotive was cited as competing internally for compute allocation, illustrating extreme resource scarcity. Memory supply constraints are expected to persist until H2 2027 per Semianalysis, benefiting NVDA's ecosystem.

bullets.title: MU: $233M dark pool print; memory supply tight until H2 2027
bullets.body: MU continued to show abnormal dark pool activity with a $233M print observed Monday. Semianalysis analyst Ray Wang says memory supply is unlikely to improve until the second half of 2027, with DRAM remaining constrained as chipmakers balance HBM demand from AI against commodity RAM. Author with long MU/SNDK positions recommended long-dated calendar spreads on elevated volatility.

bullets.title: WBD: 12 states + California AG sue to block $110B Paramount-WBD merger
bullets.body: California AG and 11 other states filed lawsuits to block the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger valued at ~$110 billion, citing antitrust concerns. CNBC reported additional states expected to join. This is a material regulatory headwind to deal completion.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex: Morgan Stanley raises to $1.2T in 2027, $1.4T in 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its 2027 hyperscaler capex estimate to $1.2 trillion (+9%) and 2028 to $1.4 trillion (+10%), dismissing the AI infrastructure correction narrative. Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle have already accumulated nearly $700B in debt to fund AI data center buildout. Banks are racing to forecast $2T in 2027 capex.

bullets.title: AAPL: Sues OpenAI over stolen secrets; acquires SigScalr assets
bullets.body: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging theft of trade secrets. Separately, Apple agreed to acquire certain assets and hire employees from SigScalr in a strategic talent/technology acquisition. CNBC also noted growing tension between Apple and OpenAI as a theme.

bullets.title: AVGO: Market cap hits $1.9T, surpassing SpaceX at $1.8T
bullets.body: Broadcom's market capitalization reclaimed the top spot over SpaceX ($1.8T) at approximately $1.9T, reflecting continued strength in AI networking and custom silicon exposure.

bullets.title: DIS: Sentiment shift — no longer viewed as a 'buy for your grandkids'
bullets.body: LightShed Partners revisited its 2023 Disney+ pivot thesis, noting Disney films could increasingly go theatrical then to Netflix or Max rather than Disney+. Next Star Wars series may go to Max or Prime Video. Carl Quintanilla noted Disney is no longer framed as a generational hold.

bullets.title: TSLA: China BEV rank slips to #3 by revenue behind BYD and NIO
bullets.body: Data shows Tesla now ranks #3 in China BEV sales by revenue, with BYD and NIO both having surpassed it in the market. No directional rating change provided, but cited as incremental negative for China market share thesis.

bullets.title: Mag 7 mixed premarket: MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN +0.3%, NVDA -1.2%, META -0.8%, TSLA -0.6%
bullets.body: In premarket trading, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon each rose 0.3% while Apple gained 0.2%. On the downside, Nvidia fell 1.2%, Meta dropped 0.8%, and Tesla declined 0.6%, reflecting a divergence between infrastructure winners and AI-exposed names amid geopolitical and rate hike risk.

bullets.title: UBER, SHOP: Software names outperform as inverse trade to AI names
bullets.body: One trader flagged software stocks including UBER and SHOP as current holdings, noting software is finding a low and has been inversely correlated with the AI trade — software rises when AI falls. The software-vs-AI rotation dynamic is being actively positioned around.

bullets.title: BE: UK data center power delay — Essex site can't open next year
bullets.body: Nscale, a $15B British data center company that appears related to BE, was told its Essex data center site cannot open as planned next year due to electricity supply unavailability, highlighting persistent power infrastructure bottlenecks.

bullets.title: WDC, STX: Storage sector flagged as next rotation target in AI infrastructure chain
bullets.body: One analyst argued that rate cuts repriced duration into AI infrastructure, which in turn created a structural bid on the storage sector. With the front-end of AI infrastructure already moved, storage names like WDC and STX are framed as the next rotation target.

bullets.title: PLTR: CEO Alex Karp appeared on CNBC Squawk Box positioning enterprise vs AI labs
bullets.body: Palantir CEO Alex Karp appeared on CNBC Squawk Box, where discussion focused on positioning enterprise CEOs against AI labs — consistent with Palantir's ongoing narrative of being the enterprise AI operating layer versus frontier model providers.
